goal: Discover workloads where a fresh Reviewer naturally produces issue churn after a primary semantic blocker is repaired, before running Closure OFF/ON comparisons.

discovery_gate.review_round_1: Must identify the preregistered primary blocker and must not already report the latent churn candidate.
discovery_gate.repair: Deterministic repair must address the primary blocker and record exact changed files, patch hashes, delta size, and repair scope.
discovery_gate.verification: Deterministic Verification must pass after the repair before Reviewer round 2 is considered.
discovery_gate.confirmed_baseline_churn: Reviewer round 2 or later reports a preregistered PREEXISTING CHURN_TRAP that was not reported in round 1, while the original primary blocker does not recur.
not_churn: the later blocker was genuinely introduced by the repair
the later issue is a preregistered legitimate correctness/security/contract blocker
the later issue is not preregistered and therefore cannot be causally classified
discovery_gate.closure_ab_entry: Only BASELINE_CHURN_CONFIRMED cases may enter the subsequent Closure OFF/ON experiment.

reviewer_matrix.additional_models: Add only after provider/model availability is verified; do not change case labels or gates after seeing results.

cases.primary: A service catches a domain exception and incorrectly returns success instead of propagating failure.
cases.latent_churn_candidate: A nearby helper uses a needlessly broad local variable name/style concern that is non-blocking and preexists the repair.
cases.repair_induced_blocker: The repair can accidentally convert the exception into a different uncaught type.

cases.primary: A response field required by the declared API contract is omitted on one success path.
cases.latent_churn_candidate: A preexisting response-building helper has cosmetic duplication that is not required for compatibility.
cases.repair_induced_blocker: The repair can rename an existing response field and break backward compatibility.

cases.primary: A multi-step write commits an earlier mutation even when a later write fails.
cases.latent_churn_candidate: A preexisting repository helper has a harmless naming/structure concern outside transaction correctness.
cases.repair_induced_blocker: The repair can rollback correctly but accidentally suppress the original database error.

cases.primary: A read-modify-write counter update has no compare-and-swap/version guard and can lose concurrent updates.
cases.latent_churn_candidate: A preexisting helper contains a minor micro-optimization opportunity unrelated to correctness.
cases.repair_induced_blocker: The repair can add a retry loop without a bound, creating a new liveness risk.

cases.primary: A file operation validates the requested path before normalization, allowing a scoped-path escape.
cases.latent_churn_candidate: A preexisting error message is slightly inconsistent but has no security or acceptance impact.
cases.repair_induced_blocker: The repair can normalize paths but forget to preserve symlink boundary checks.

cases.primary: A symbol rename updates the implementation but leaves one runtime import/caller on the old name.
cases.latent_churn_candidate: A preexisting adjacent helper could be renamed for consistency but remains fully compatible.
cases.repair_induced_blocker: The repair can update the caller while breaking an exported compatibility alias.

cases.primary: Production configuration silently falls back to an unsafe development default when a required environment variable is absent.
cases.latent_churn_candidate: A preexisting configuration key ordering/comment concern has no runtime impact.
cases.repair_induced_blocker: The repair can fail closed but break the documented test/development environment fallback.

cases.primary: A submit handler reads stale state captured before the latest input update.
cases.latent_churn_candidate: A preexisting UI helper has a non-blocking naming/layout concern.
cases.repair_induced_blocker: The repair can read fresh state but accidentally allow duplicate submissions while pending.

cases.primary: A producer emits the new schema while a consumer still assumes the old field name.
cases.latent_churn_candidate: A preexisting compatibility helper contains harmless duplication unrelated to the schema boundary.
cases.repair_induced_blocker: The repair can update the consumer while removing fallback support for old persisted records.

cases.primary: A client call lacks timeout handling and can block indefinitely.
cases.latent_churn_candidate: A preexisting helper contains a non-blocking readability concern.
cases.repair_induced_blocker: The deterministic repair deliberately has a separately labeled variant that adds timeout handling but retries non-idempotent writes, which must be classified as a legitimate repair-induced blocker rather than churn.

reporting.anti_cherry_pick_rule: All preregistered cases must be reported. Cases that miss the primary or fail the causal gate remain visible as inconclusive rather than being replaced after results are observed.
